FOR CLAT 2027
7

QUAD FM Meeting


• The foreign ministers of the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad)
  met at Hyderabad House in New Delhi on 26 May 2026 to
  launch a series of major initiatives.

• External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar chaired the session, which
  focused on maritime surveillance, port infrastructure, critical minerals,
  and regional energy security.

• US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the meeting’s
  outcomes as “real concrete achievables”, highlighting the Quad’s
  transformation into a “partnership of action”.

QUAD FM Meeting

What is the QUAD? –

• The Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad) started as an informal
  partnership after the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, when India,
  Australia, Japan and the US coordinated humanitarian and disaster
  relief.

• It was officially proposed by former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo
  Abe in 2007, but became inactive for almost a decade due to
  Australian concerns about provoking China.

• The Quad was revived in 2017 reflecting evolving regional views on
  China’s expanding influence, and has since held multiple foreign
  ministers’ meetings and leaders’ summits.

QUAD FM Meeting


• September 2021: The then US President Biden hosted the first in-
  person Quad Leaders’ Summit in Washington with PM Modi, PM
  Morrison and PM Suga.

• May 2023: The then Australian PM Albanese hosted the Quad
  Leaders’ Summit in Hiroshima with PM Modi, PM Kishida and
  President Biden.

• Since 2019, the Quad foreign ministers have gathered eight times,
  with five top-level summits held since March 2021.

QUAD FM Meeting


• The Quad aims to counterbalance China’s growing geopolitical
  and economic influence in the Indo-Pacific region by presenting a
  united front of democratic nations.

• It seeks to ensure security and freedom of navigation in critical
  maritime routes, such as the South China Sea, which are essential for
  international trade.

• The group focuses on fostering economic development,
  infrastructure projects, technology innovation, and
  addressing global challenges like pandemics and climate change.

QUAD FM Meeting


• Approximately one-third of the world’s shipping passes through
  the South China Sea, which is rich in fish and fossil fuels, making it a
  strategic zone contested by regional powers.

• China claims over 80% of the South China Sea based on
  the “nine-dash line” , overlapping with internationally recognised
  territories of Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia and the
  Philippines.

• The Quad has consistently opposed “intimidating manoeuvres”
  and the militarisation of disputed features, reaffirming adherence to
  the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), 1982.

QUAD FM Meeting

Quad Plus –

• It refers to the expansion of the Quad dialogue to include other
  like-minded countries on specific issues, such as South Korea,
  Vietnam, and New Zealand, who joined weekly Quad meetings in
  March 2020.

• In May 2020, the US hosted a meeting with Quad nations along
  with Brazil, Israel and South Korea to discuss a global response
  to COVID-19.

• Quad Plus focuses on global issues like pandemics, whereas the
  Quad deals primarily with security concerns in maritime,
  technology and infrastructure.

QUAD FM Meeting


• Quad Plus provides a multipolar perspective for examining and
  evaluating the strategic multilateral expansion of the participating
  nations.

• It could lay the groundwork for future expansion or
  collaborations in the region.

• Quad Plus links the four founding nations with emerging global
  powers through initiatives that support regional prosperity, peace,
  and stability.

QUAD FM Meeting


IMPDA –

• The Indo-Pacific Maritime Domain Awareness was launched at
  the 2022 Quad Leaders’ Summit in Tokyo to enhance maritime
  domain awareness capabilities in the Indo-Pacific region.

• It is a technology and training initiative that provides
  near-real-time commercial satellite tracking data to countries across
  Southeast Asia, the Indian Ocean region, and the Pacific.

• The Quad has initiated regional pilots to deliver radio frequency
  data to maritime agencies, helping combat illegal fishing, trafficking
  and supporting humanitarian disaster response.

QUAD FM Meeting


• On September 21, 2024, US President Biden hosted PM Modi, PM
  Albanese, and PM Kishida in Wilmington, Delaware, after India
  swapped hosting rights.

• The summit launched the Quad Cancer Moonshot, MAITRI, Quad
  Ports of the Future Partnership, a 2025 Quad-at-Sea Mission, and a
  semiconductor supply chain network.

• Leaders committed to securing Quad funding, creating a US
  Congressional Quad Caucus, and holding the first Quad Commerce
  and Industry Ministers meeting.

QUAD FM Meeting


India – Japan Bilateral Exercises

• Malabar Exercise: Naval drills involving India, Japan, the US (and
  Australia) for maritime security and interoperability.

• Dharma Guardian: Annual counter-terrorism exercise between the
  Indian and Japanese armies.

• Shinyuu Maitri: Air force exercise focusing on air defence, disaster
  response and humanitarian assistance.

QUAD FM Meeting


India – Australia Bilateral Exercises

• AUSINDEX: Joint naval exercise focusing on maritime operations,
  anti-submarine warfare and security.

• PITCH BLACK: Air force exercise enhancing tactical air operations
  and interoperability among participating nations.

• TAHWEI: Army exercise involving training in counter-terrorism and
  peacekeeping operations.

QUAD FM Meeting


India – US Bilateral Exercises

• Yudh Abhyas: Army counter-terrorism training exercise held
  annually.

• Vajra Prahar: Special forces counter-terrorism exercise focused on
  joint planning and operations.

• Cope India: Air combat training exercise between the Indian and US
  Air Forces.

• Tiger Triumph: Joint tri-service disaster relief exercise.

QUAD FM Meeting

Recent Meeting –

• It was attended by EAM S. Jaishankar (India), US Secretary of
  State Marco Rubio, Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong, and
  Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi.

• This was the third Quad Foreign Ministers’ meeting in a short
  span (January 2025, July 2025, and now May 2026), demonstrating
  the group’s sustained engagement.

• The ministers devoted a large part of their exchanges to analysing
  the “current state of the world” , with a specific focus on the
  Indo-Pacific.

QUAD FM Meeting


• The Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Corporation initiative
  was launched to leverage each country’s surveillance assets to
  enhance information sharing.

• The IPMDA was expanded to the Indian Ocean, providing
  near-real-time unclassified satellite tracking data to combat illegal
  fishing, trafficking, and support disaster response.

• India committed to hosting the next Quad at Sea Mission, bringing
  together coast guards of all four nations on a single ship.

QUAD FM Meeting


• The Quad announced its first-ever joint port infrastructure
  project under the Quad Ports of the Future Partnership, with a pilot
  project to advance port infrastructure in Fiji.

• This directly addresses insufficient port capacity in the Pacific Islands
  and is a practical demonstration of the Quad’s ability to deliver
  high-quality, resilient infrastructure.

• It is expected to serve as a model for other projects in the region
  in the future.

QUAD FM Meeting


• The ministers launched the Quad Critical Minerals
  Initiative framework to strengthen supply chains for critical
  minerals, including mining, processing and recycling.

• The initiative aims to coordinate investment and leverage
  economic policy tools to reduce dependence on single sources
  (implicitly China).

• It reflects growing concern over the export restrictions of critical
  minerals by certain countries, which can destabilise global supply
  chains.

QUAD FM Meeting


• The Quad initiative on Indo-Pacific energy security was
  announced to strengthen regional energy resilience, especially in light
  of the Iranian closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

• The partners will identify areas of cooperation in technology,
  management, policy, market analysis and emergency
  response exercises.

• The US Department of Energy will host a fuel security forum later
  in 2026 to further expand on this initiative.

QUAD FM Meeting


• The joint statement after the meeting did not identify the host
  country for the next leaders’ Summit (which was due to be held
  in India), sparking speculation about the group’s future.

• Officials cited difficulty in pinning down leaders’ schedules,
  with the Summit possibly being held on the sidelines of other
  multilateral meetings like the UN General Assembly or G-20
  Summit in the US in December.

• Australia will now host the next Foreign Ministers’ meeting, as
  India will hand over the chair of the grouping.

QUAD FM Meeting


• China has consistently opposed the Quad, describing it as an attempt
  to create “exclusive small cliques” that undermine regional
  cooperation.

• Beijing views the Quad as a US-led containment strategy aimed
  at countering its rise, and has warned against the militarisation of the
  South China Sea.

• Despite Quad statements, China continues to assert its claims in
  the South China Sea and has increased its maritime militia activities
  in the region.

The controversy surrounding the Delhi Gymkhana Club in 2026 has reignited debate over land
governance, elite institutions, and public property regulation in India. The Union government
sought repossession of the club premises situated in Lutyens’ Delhi, citing lease,
administrative, and public land considerations. The move triggered legal proceedings and
wider discussion regarding the use of government land by private institutions.


The Delhi Gymkhana Club, established during the colonial period, occupies a prominent site in
New Delhi and has historically been associated with senior bureaucrats, military officers,
diplomats, and business elites. The dispute has raised broader questions concerning leasehold
rights, transparency, accountability, and regulation of organisations occupying public land.

Source: Indian Express

Lutyens’ Delhi, associated with the Delhi Gymkhana Club controversy, is
named after:

A. Herbert Lutyens
B. Edwin Lutyens
C. Robert Tor Lutyens
D. Charles Lutyens
ANSWER - B

New Delhi was officially inaugurated as the capital of British India in:

A. 1858
B. 1911
C. 1931
D. 1947
ANSWER - C

“Land” as a legislative subject in the Indian Constitution falls primarily
under:

A. Union List
B. Concurrent List
C. State List
D. Residuary Powers
ANSWER - C

Consider the following:

A: Lease disputes may arise even when the government owns the
underlying land.

B: Lutyens’ Delhi was planned during the colonial period.

A. Only A
B. Only B
C. Both A and B
D. Neither A nor B
ANSWER - C

PASSAGE:

The QUAD Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held in 2026 brought together ______________ to
discuss regional security, maritime cooperation, supply-chain resilience, and developments
in the Indo-Pacific region. The meeting gained significance amid growing concerns
regarding geopolitical tensions, energy security, critical minerals, and maritime stability.
New initiatives relating to infrastructure, maritime coordination, and resilient supply
chains were discussed by the member states.

The QUAD, formally known as the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue, is an informal strategic
grouping that has emerged as an important platform for cooperation among major Indo-
Pacific democracies. Although not a military alliance, the grouping frequently addresses
issues such as maritime security, technological cooperation, disaster relief, and regional
connectivity.

Source: Indian Express

The QUAD consists of which of the following four countries?

A. India, China, Japan, Australia
B. India, USA, Japan, Australia
C. USA, UK, India, Japan
D. India, France, USA, Australia
ANSWER - B

The QUAD was first initiated in:

A. 2001
B. 2005
C. 2007
D. 2010
ANSWER - C

The QUAD is most closely associated with developments in the:

A. Mediterranean region
B. Indo-Pacific region
C. Arctic region
D. Latin American region
ANSWER - B

Consider the following:

A: The QUAD is a formal military alliance similar to NATO.

B: India is a member of the QUAD.

A. Only A
B. Only B
C. Both A and B
D. Neither A nor B
ANSWER - B

In 2026, Assam passed a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill, becoming one of the few
Indian states to legislate on the issue of common civil laws. The legislation triggered
political, constitutional, and social debate regarding personal laws, gender justice,
religious freedom, and federal powers. The law includes provisions relating to
marriage, divorce, succession, and related civil matters.

The debate around the UCC has long occupied an important place in Indian
constitutional discourse. Supporters argue that a common civil framework promotes
equality and uniformity in personal laws, while critics raise concerns regarding
religious autonomy, cultural diversity, and minority protections. The subject also
intersects with constitutional principles relating to secularism and Directive Principles
of State Policy.

Source: The Hindu

The concept of a Uniform Civil Code is mentioned in which part of the Indian
Constitution?

A. Fundamental Rights
B. Fundamental Duties
C. Directive Principles of State Policy
D. Emergency Provisions
ANSWER - C

The constitutional provision relating to the Uniform Civil Code is:

A. Article 21
B. Article 32
C. Article 42
D. Article 44
ANSWER - D

Before Assam’s move, which state became the first Indian state to enact a
Uniform Civil Code law?

A. Gujarat
B. Goa
C. Uttarakhand
D. Maharashtra
ANSWER - C

A Uniform Civil Code generally deals with matters relating to:

A. Criminal offences and policing in a particular state
B. Personal civil matters such as marriage and inheritance
C. Taxation and customs duties relating to religion and castes
D. Banking regulation
ANSWER - B

In which year was the Goa UCC passed?

A. 1867
B. 1892
C. 1917
D. 1947
ANSWER - A

PASSAGE:

India received its fourth squadron of the _________-origin S-400 Triumf air defence
missile system in 2026, marking another major step in strengthening the country’s
air defence capabilities. The S-400 system is regarded as one of the world’s most
advanced long-range surface-to-air missile defence systems and is designed to
detect, track, and intercept a variety of aerial threats.

India’s acquisition of the S-400 has attracted international attention because of its
strategic significance and the geopolitical implications of defence cooperation with
________. The system is intended to enhance India’s layered air defence
architecture amid evolving regional security concerns. It is capable of engaging
aircraft, drones, cruise missiles, and certain ballistic missile threats over long
distances.

Source: The Hindu

The S-400 Triumf system acquired by India is primarily a:

A. Main battle tank
B. Air defence system
C. Nuclear submarine
D. Fighter aircraft
ANSWER - B

The S-400 Triumf system is manufactured by:

A. France
B. United States
C. Russia
D. Israel
ANSWER - C

India’s purchase of the S-400 system has often been discussed in relation to
which country’s sanctions framework?

A. Germany
B. Japan
C. United States
D. Brazil
ANSWER - C

In which year was the contract signed between India and Russia for 5
squadrons of S-400?

A. 2018
B. 2020
C. 2016
D. 2022
ANSWER - A

In 2026, BRICS countries collectively endorsed stronger international recognition of
Palestinian statehood, renewing calls for a two-state solution and wider diplomatic
acceptance of Palestine in international forums. The development gained geopolitical
significance because BRICS has expanded its influence in global governance discussions,
often presenting itself as a voice of the Global South on issues relating to sovereignty,
multilateralism, and reform of international institutions.

The declaration emerged amid continuing conflict in West Asia and debates regarding
ceasefire arrangements, humanitarian access, and recognition of Palestinian political rights.
International reactions varied, reflecting longstanding divisions regarding recognition,
security concerns, territorial disputes, and the future status of Jerusalem.


Source: Al Jazeera

Palestine currently holds which status in the United Nations system?

A. Full Member State
B. Permanent Observer State
C. Associate Security Council Member
D. Non-Member Observer State
ANSWER - D

Which of the following best reflects the dominant legal criterion associated
with statehood under the Montevideo Convention?

A. Military superiority, capacity for foreign relations and Legitimate
Government
B. Permanent population, territory, government, and capacity for foreign
relations
C. Recognition by all permanent UNSC members
D. Membership in the United Nations
ANSWER - B

Which of the following countries joined BRICS during the 2024 expansion
round?

A. Turkey
B. Indonesia
C. Ethiopia
D. Pakistan
ANSWER - C

Recognition of a state by other countries is most directly associated with
which concept of international law?

A. Jus cogens
B. Diplomatic recognition
C. Universal jurisdiction
D. Extradition principle
ANSWER - B

Which of the following best explains why BRICS involvement in the Palestine
issue is geopolitically significant?

A. BRICS functions as a chief negotiator in the UN to resolve the Israel-
Palestine conflict.
B. BRICS increasingly seeks influence in global governance and Global South
diplomacy.
C. BRICS possesses treaty authority over West Asian borders, and thus has
major advantage in GDP.
D. BRICS controls admission to the UN Security Council.
ANSWER - B
